headline: Tech stocks dragged US markets last night while the ASX held up today, but your portfolio is sitting almost exactly at breakeven — down just $2.62 overall.

portfolio.summary: Your portfolio sits at $1,908 AUD, basically dead flat against your $1,911 invested — you're down just $2.62 in total, which is as close to breakeven as it gets. The big story is your US tech holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) all fell last night in USD terms, but the Aussie dollar is steady at 71.65 US cents so there's no currency cushion right now. On the bright side, GOOG is still your standout winner — you're up $16.75 AUD (24%) since you bought in. TTWO is the biggest dollar drag at -$19.89 AUD (-4.07%), and FUEL.AX had a nice day today, up 1.75% to close at $8.70. Your ASX ETFs (VDHG, VTS) were all modestly green today.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Fell USD $14.19 last night to $358.39. Still your best-performing position overall — up $16.75 AUD (24%) since you bought in. The drop appears linked to broader negative sentiment around Google lagging OpenAI and Anthropic in the AI race.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Biggest percentage drop last night, down USD $19.21 to $441.31. In AUD terms you're almost exactly at your buy-in price — down just $1.59. Microsoft unveiled new in-house AI models to reduce reliance on OpenAI, which may have spooked some investors short-term.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Down USD $4.60 last night to $222.38. This is your biggest dollar loser at -$19.89 AUD. GTA 6 hype continues to swirl but no major news catalyst — just general tech selling pressure.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: Best ASX mover today, up $0.15 to close at $8.70. Oil prices surged over 2% last night on Iran-US tensions and Middle East conflict, lifting energy stocks. You're now up $5.73 AUD (2.86%) on this one.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: Closed up $2.38 today at $522.55. Up $2.99 AUD overall since you bought in. Steady performance tracking the broad US market.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Fell $0.12 today to $6.43. Down $6.90 AUD (-4.6%) since you bought in. Despite bullish lithium price commentary from Citi today, the stock couldn't hold ground. Lithium sentiment is improving but PLS is still underwater for you.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a solid session today, closing up 0.7% at 8,785. Last night's US session was basically flat — the S&P 500 edged up 0.13% and the NASDAQ barely moved (+0.03%), masking the fact that big tech names like MSFT and GOOG sold off hard individually. Oil is the real mover — WTI crude jumped 2.09% to $95.72 a barrel on Middle East tensions involving Iran. Gold is steady at $4,491. The Aussie dollar is essentially unchanged at 71.65 US cents.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night — near flat, masking big individual tech losses.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Last night — essentially flat despite MSFT and GOOG selling off.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Surging on Iran-US strikes and Middle East conflict.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Barely moved — holding near all-time highs.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Dead flat — no currency tailwind or headwind today.

politics.summary: Big economic news today — Australia's GDP is growing at 2.5% annually but the pace is slowing, and there are fresh questions about whether the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) has any room left to keep raising interest rates. The housing market is also in focus, with both the RBA and Treasurer Chalmers pointing fingers at high rates and taxes as the culprit for falling house prices.

stories.title: Australia's economy growing at 2.5% but the slowdown is real
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's economy grew 2.5% over the past year but economists say the momentum is fading fast. The combination of high interest rates biting into household budgets and cost-of-living pressure is starting to show up in the numbers. For everyday Aussies, this means growth is positive but increasingly fragile — and for the RBA, it makes further rate hikes look increasingly risky.

stories.title: Stalling economy could stop further RBA rate hikes
stories.why_it_matters: Analysts are now openly questioning whether the RBA can justify any more interest rate increases given the weakening economy. The argument is simple: if the economy is already slowing down on its own, raising rates further risks tipping Australia into a more serious downturn. This is good news for mortgage holders who've been hoping for relief, and it's why markets are now pricing in fewer future rate hikes.

stories.title: RBA and Chalmers blame rates and tax for falling house prices
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA and Treasurer Jim Chalmers are now publicly acknowledging that high interest rates and tax settings are behind the drop in house prices. This is a notable admission — it suggests policymakers are aware the medicine (rate hikes) is hurting the housing market. For property owners on the Gold Coast, it's a mixed signal: prices may keep softening if rates stay high, but the acknowledgement from the top suggests relief could be coming.

stories.title: Labor MPs asked to personally fund campaign to salvage the budget
stories.why_it_matters: Labor MPs are reportedly being asked to reach into their own pockets to fund a public relations campaign to shore up the budget's reputation. This suggests the government is feeling serious pressure over its fiscal management and is struggling to sell its economic story to voters. It's an unusual move that signals internal concern about how the budget is landing politically.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is a Trump executive order (a directive from the President) that creates a 'pre-clearance' process for major AI models from OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic before they launch. Meanwhile, a prominent tech commentator made waves arguing Google is genuinely falling behind in the AI race, and Microsoft unveiled new home-grown AI models to cut costs and reduce its dependence on OpenAI.

stories.title: Trump orders government pre-checks on AI models before they launch
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration is setting up a process where major AI labs — OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic — must get a kind of government tick-of-approval before releasing new AI models to the public. It's being framed as a national security measure rather than a consumer protection rule. Critics argue this is too little (no real regulation, just a check-in process), while some in the industry worry it could slow down US AI development relative to China. For Google (GOOG) and Microsoft (MSFT), this adds a layer of bureaucracy to future product launches.

stories.title: Google is falling behind OpenAI and Anthropic — and it could be 'company-destroying'
stories.why_it_matters: Prominent tech analyst M.G. Siegler published a sharp critique arguing Google is genuinely losing ground to OpenAI and Anthropic in the race to make AI a standalone product people actually use day-to-day — not just a search add-on. His argument is that Google built AI as a feature to protect Search, while its rivals built AI as the whole product. He calls the strategic misstep potentially 'company-destroying' if Google can't adapt. This is directly relevant to your GOOG holding and likely contributed to last night's share price drop.

stories.title: Microsoft unveils new home-grown AI models to cut costs and reduce OpenAI reliance
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft has unveiled a suite of its own internally-developed AI models, explicitly designed to reduce how much it pays OpenAI and make AI tools cheaper for developers to build with. This is a big strategic move — Microsoft has invested billions in OpenAI but is now hedging its bets by building its own AI stack. For developers, it means cheaper, more flexible tools. For MSFT investors, it signals the company is trying to protect its margins as AI infrastructure costs soar. Short-term the stock sold off, but the long-term logic is sound.

stories.title: Google competing for $80 billion in investor money as big AI IPOs loom
stories.why_it_matters: As AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic gear up for potential IPOs (stock market listings), Google finds itself in an unusual position: it's now competing with its own AI rivals for the same pool of investor dollars. The article estimates up to $80 billion in capital could flow into standalone AI companies, money that might otherwise prop up Alphabet's valuation. It's another headwind for GOOG — investors may increasingly see pure-play AI startups as more exciting bets than a legacy tech giant trying to retrofit AI into its existing products.

sport.summary: NRL Round 14 kicks off tomorrow night. Big coaching and signing news in the league today, plus the AFL mid-season report cards are out. Wimbledon is also in the news with players pushing back on prize money.

stories.title: Kieran Foran named Manly Sea Eagles head coach
stories.why_it_matters: Kieran Foran — the former Manly, Warriors and Bulldogs halfback — has been appointed as the Sea Eagles' new head coach. Foran gets the top job at 4 Pines Park just as Manly prepare to host the Rabbitohs in tomorrow night's Round 14 opener. The ABC also reports an Origin rep signed with two clubs in one day, suggesting some player movement chaos at the mid-point of the season.

stories.title: NRL mid-season report cards: Who's up, who's down at the halfway point
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports has published its mid-season NRL report cards, grading every team on their first half of the 2026 season. The piece calls out a 'staggering reality for a fallen contender' and highlights truths that coach Jason Ryles 'can't hide from' — pointing to the Raiders as a team underperforming expectations. Round 14 kicks off tomorrow night with Sea Eagles v Rabbitohs.

stories.title: Tigers star warns 'I'll never be loyal to a club' — and Benji Marshall is at the centre of it
stories.why_it_matters: A Wests Tigers player has made a blunt public statement that he'll 'never be loyal to a club', and Fox Sports reports that coach Benji Marshall is central to the contract drama. The Tigers host the Panthers in Round 14 on Sunday, adding extra spice to what's already a messy mid-season at Concord. The comment is a shot across the bow as the club tries to retain key players.

stories.title: AFL mid-season report cards: Every club graded at the halfway point
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL's official website has published mid-season grades for all 18 clubs, highlighting the best players, biggest surprises and disappointments so far in 2026. Separately, an Essendon Bombers player has received a wave of support from the AFL community after some 'shattering' personal news came to light — though details remain vague in reporting so far.

stories.title: Wimbledon could be next in player revolt over prize money
stories.why_it_matters: Wimbledon may be the next Grand Slam to face a player backlash over prize money distribution, according to The Telegraph. Players have been increasingly vocal about the gap between top earners and early-round losers at major tournaments. With Wimbledon approaching, pressure is building on the All England Club to address the disparity before it becomes a full-blown controversy.
